surface_a.description: a gate that binds an instrument's derived answer to a digest of the bytes it read

findings.mechanism: capture embeds raw adapter stdout and computes RECEIPT-SHA256=<64hex> covering all preceding header bytes; verify recomputes digest of body above the sha line (RECEIPT-DIGEST-MISMATCH), re-derives counts from embedded output (RECEIPT-COUNT-MISMATCH), and checks script sha256 drift (RECEIPT-SCRIPT-DRIFT).
findings.verdict: Not contested: souji owns census-run receipts and sources-census validation; Kumitate's C1 binds arm counter transcripts and counter source call sites.

findings.mechanism: Re-derives every derived boolean and verdict from the raw observation of a retained context receipt byte-pinned by expected.receipt_sha256; verifies sha256(receipt_bytes) == expected.receipt_sha256 and recomputed verdict equals expected.id / expected.exit.
findings.verdict: Not contested: tameshi re-derives raw context receipts, whereas Kumitate binds arm-form counter transcripts.

findings.mechanism: Scans receipts for # tool_sha256: <64 hex> and # measured_rev: <rev>, asserting sha256(git cat-file blob <measured_rev>:<tool>) == tool_sha256.
findings.verdict: Not contested: tameshi verifies that historical tool SHAs exist in git blobs across evidence files; Kumitate reconciles live/fixture arm transcripts against probe source call sites.

findings.mechanism: Binds claims in a measurement manifest to the sha256 blob digest of the counter script at the measured revision (counter.sha256), asserting counter_digest_mismatch if blob != sha256.
findings.verdict: Not contested: tabi binds measurement manifest JSON metadata to git blobs, not arm counter transcripts.

findings.mechanism: Extracts all 64-hex sha256 pins from a receipt and checks each against sha256 of committed blob bytes in the git object database.
findings.verdict: Not contested: chousa verifies object database existence of pinned hashes, not counter transcript reconciliation.

findings.mechanism: Evaluates tsukuroi-census.sh --identity, asserting the running bash script prints its own sha256, md5, bytes, and lines, checking against the counter's own calculation over the script file bytes.
findings.verdict: Not contested: tsukuroi tests self-fingerprinting of a shell script, not counter transcript checkers.

surface_b.description: a corpus index gate that is section-blind (counts | rows anywhere)

findings.mechanism: index_rows(readme) splits corpus/README.md lines and matches any line starting with | whose first cell matches FIRST_CELL = r'`(knowledge|lessons)/([^`]+)`' without section heading boundary checks.
findings.verdict: Contested mechanism: kengaku used a section-blind table row counter in a round-75 plan probe; not an active gating script in scripts/ or tools/.

findings.mechanism: Scans corpus/README.md for markdown tables; triggers in_map when table header row has row[0].lower() == 'ground' and row[2].lower().startswith('entries'). It is section-blind (does not check ## headings), but table-header scoped.
findings.verdict: Not contested: souji scopes by table column headers (ground/entries), whereas Kumitate's readme-map.mjs was completely section-blind and header-blind.

findings.mechanism: Section-aware corpus index auditor. Explicitly matches SECTION_RE = re.compile(r'^## ([a-z-]+)/ \((\d+)\)\s*$', re.M) and restricts row extraction strictly between section start and the next ## heading.
findings.verdict: Not contested (contrast finding): kotodama avoided section-blindness by design, using heading spans.

findings.mechanism: Command A explicitly slices corpus/README.md by section: sec = readme.split('## Coverage map\n', 1)[1].split('\n## ', 1)[0], isolating only rows inside ## Coverage map.
findings.verdict: Not contested (contrast finding): kaidoku implemented explicit section slicing to prevent section-blindness.

findings.mechanism: Explicitly bounds audit to section heading: HEADING = '## Coverage map — round 35 addition'; lines outside that heading are ignored.
findings.verdict: Not contested (contrast finding): kama strictly checks heading presence and scope.

findings.mechanism: Section-blind path scanner (G02). Uses regex search across the normalized full text of corpus/README.md to ensure every corpus/knowledge/*.md file name appears somewhere, and checks phantom paths against all regex matches.
findings.verdict: Not contested: chousa is section-blind but does not count table rows (matches filename tokens anywhere in prose).
